podcast.title: Plov for breakfast

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: How do you usually celebrate New Year? Guess: what did Leyla eat for breakfast after the party?

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is holidays and celebrations. And Leyla had a big party last weekend.
[laugh] Not my party — my parents'. It was their thirtieth wedding anniversary.
Thirty years! Congratulations to them. How did you celebrate?
A big family gathering at their house. We invited about forty people. My mum said, "The more the merrier!"
Forty people at home? Who cooked?
Everyone! My aunts brought plov, dolma, salads, cakes… It was a real feast.
That sounds amazing. And what happened to all the food?
We're still eating the leftovers. I had plov for breakfast today.
[chuckle] Lucky you. In my family, Christmas leftovers last a week. Turkey sandwiches every day.
Speaking of big holidays — this year you'll spend New Year in Baku, right?
Yes! I'm excited. What's the tradition here?
New Year is huge here. We decorate a tree with lights and toys, and the whole family sits at the table until midnight.
In England, a lot of people go out to ring in the new year with friends — in pubs, or in the street.
Here it's more about family. But at midnight, everyone goes to the window or the balcony to watch the fireworks over the sea.
Fireworks over the sea. That must be beautiful.
It is. And then, at about one in the morning, the young people go out and visit their friends.
So the party never ends!
[laugh] Not until the second of January.
Then I'd better start practising. Eating, I mean.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: what is your favourite celebration of the year, and how does your family spend it?
Mine will be New Year in Baku. See you next time!
Bye for now!
